steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 MEASURED, twice, superseding this step's stale note (~5.8 dmg/hit -- damage was rebalanced since it was written). Quick attacks land ~12-13.4; the charged lands ~56; the practice bramblebun rolls 104-124 HP depending on the boot. RUN6 attempt 1 ran 6 quick then the charged: 104.3 -> 91.3 -> 78.0 -> 63.8 -> 49.4 -> 0.0, the charged FAINTED it and the catch had nothing to throw at. Attempt 2 ran 1 quick then the charged, the charged missed (cone 75 deg, range 3.0, the target had moved), the throw went at 90% HP where `catching.json`'s hp_factor is 0.10, and it failed. The retry blocks below re-enter `combat_aim` (the telemetry shows ctx=combat_aim on each retry press) but NO second `catch_throw` is ever emitted -- three retries, three re-aims, zero throws, across two runs. Recorded as an open defect (GAME-11/RIG-26); it means the `max_catch_failures: 1` guarantee, which only bites on the SECOND landed throw, is currently unreachable. steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6: `data/config/opening.json` sets `max_catch_failures: 1` and its own comment quotes docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md -- 'the tutorial catch cannot fail twice'. The bound counts LANDED throws, so the game's promise is kept on the SECOND landed throw, not the first. This segment threw exactly once and read the resulting party of 1 as a defect. RUN6's attempt 2 produced the first `catch_throw` event in this whole effort and it failed legitimately at 90% HP. These retry blocks are what the config's own pity bound expects a player to do, and they mirror S03-32a..j2's ten engage attempts against the same species.

steps.title: aim again (throw 4)
steps.expected: re-aim for a fourth landed throw
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6, fourth measurement. The retry blocks below re-enter `combat_aim` (the telemetry shows ctx=combat_aim on each retry press) but NO second `catch_throw` is ever emitted -- three retries, three re-aims, zero throws, across two runs. Recorded as an open defect (GAME-11/RIG-26); it means the `max_catch_failures: 1` guarantee, which only bites on the SECOND landed throw, is currently unreachable. Until that is root-caused the segment cannot rely on the pity bound, so the FIRST throw has to carry the catch: the charged attack plus three quick attacks lands ~95 damage on a creature that rolls 104-124 HP, leaving 9-29 HP (9-23%), which is high up `catching.json`'s hp_factor curve without fainting either roll.

steps.title: throw again (throw 4)
steps.expected: a fourth landed throw resolves
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6, third measurement: `combat_manager.gd:1273` applies `catch_math.apply_failure_bound()` once `_tutorial_catch_failure_bound >= 0`, so with `max_catch_failures: 1` the SECOND LANDED throw is forced to succeed. The binding constraint is therefore not catch odds -- it is keeping the fight alive long enough for two throws to land. A lvl-3 starter (117 HP) against a practice bramblebun that rolls lvl 5 / 124 HP loses a long exchange: one RUN6 run ended with Moss at 0.0 HP and the fight over before the retries could throw. So the pre-catch damage is cut to the charged attack plus a single quick (both verbs still exercised for section E.4, ~69 dmg, leaving 34-44% HP on either roll), and the throw sequence is entered sooner and retried three times.

steps.title: put away the drop confirmation the open press raised
steps.expected: B dismisses the 'Drop it? / Cancel' confirmation and leaves the shell open, which is what a player does. DEFECT RECORDED, not worked around silently: `game_menu` and `backpack_drop` are the SAME physical button -- gamepad Start, button 6 in project.godot -- so the press that opens the pause shell also fires the destructive drop verb on the backpack tab the shell opens on. tab_backpack.gd:1345-1370 already carries a guard for exactly this (`_ignore_drop_until_release`) and its comment describes this exact symptom; the guard did not hold here. Observed in S02 attempts 5 and 6: the shell opened on `menu_backpack` with focus on 'Drop it', 5x menu_tab_right never left the backpack tab, and no handoff save was written. A developer probe (tools/opening_fix/probe_tab_cycle.gd on ralph/OPENING-STARTER-FOCUS) confirms the game cycles backpack->creatures->map->quest_log->build->SAVE->settings correctly when the satchel is EMPTY, so the tab machinery is sound and the confirmation is what eats the presses.

steps.observation: settle_frames raised 12 -> 45. Attempt 5 opened the shell on `menu_backpack` with focus on 'Drop it' and five RB presses left it on `menu_backpack`, so the Save tab was never reached and no handoff save was written. A developer probe (tools/opening_fix/probe_tab_cycle.gd) shows the game cycles correctly -- backpack -> creatures -> map -> quest_log -> build -> SAVE -> settings on five presses -- in a world where the player carries nothing, at 20 frames between presses. The difference in S02 is a full satchel from Grandpa plus the map tab baking its map, which is the exact case this file's own `press` comment warns about: 'a tab switch rebuilds a whole tab body ... back-to-back presses with only the injection's own frames between them can arrive while the previous one is still being digested.'
